sourceDecisions: Exact Node 26.12.0, Node declarations 26.6.5, TypeScript 7.0.2, pnpm 12.14.0 and accepted TypeScript API alias have one JSON authority. Engine ranges and packageManager derive from that catalog.

Pure projector implements --check and --write over .nvmrc, all five existing Node engine manifests, root packageManager/pnpm engine, and both default and named TypeScript API aliases. Neither mode was executed.

Portable PowerShell/bash selectors resolve and verify the exact catalog runtime, including the active node command. No sibling repository path is embedded. Parent shells must still select and verify the main canonical runtime first.
The first-party typecheck runner resolves and compares the exact installed TypeScript CLI without yaml or the legacy .nvmrc authority.

Bootstrap readers prefer source JSON authority and reject stale manager, runtime engines, compiler, declaration and alias projections. Packed snapshots copy the same canonical JSON; all recipe engine placeholders derive from it.

Published pnpm 12.14.0 uses native binaries. The runner rejects JS/cmd/shell manager shims, resolves only existing native bytes, and probes exact manager version. No manager installation/download fallback exists.

Nested Lerna lockfile updates were inspected in published 10.1.1 source: they invoke pnpm and may route through COREPACK_ROOT. Child environments now pin the native manager directory and Node executable, clear the inherited Corepack routing variable, and reject competing pnpm shims in the selected Node directory.

Explicit repository pnpm calls in manifests, publish scripts, maintained CI checks, Turbo graph regression, and bootstrap install use the pinned runner. Existing workflow trigger/action-reference/permission values are preserved; setup-node pnpm cache lookup was removed because it invokes an ambient manager.

All four original toolchain source tests remain, strengthened by exact catalog comparisons. Added behavior coverage exercises derivations, projection repair/preservation, stale bootstrap rejection, exact runtime choice, native header/manager failure checks, child environments and nested manager shadow prevention.
